Q: Select first approved or denied row if status doesn't change. Select last row if it does change from 'approved' or 'denied' A:

If I got it right - you want to fetch just the rows with the status IN('approved', 'denied') following the rules described in question. I presume your "first row" and "last row" refer to order by STATUS_DATE.
You could exclude the rows where status is not approved or denied and use the Case expression to check is there one or more distinct STATUS(es) left per SID and flag the first or the last (Min/Max) STATUS_DATE.
This will give you the filter condition (STATUS_DATE = FLAG_DATE) to get the rows you want.

SELECT SID, STATUS, STATUS_DATE
FROM  (   Select   t.*, 
                   Case When Count(Distinct STATUS) Over(Partition By SID) = 1
                        Then Min(STATUS_DATE) Over(Partition By SID)
                  Else Max(STATUS_DATE) Over(Partition By SID)
                  End as FLAG_DATE
         From     tbl t
         Where    STATUS IN('approved', 'denied')
     )
WHERE     STATUS_DATE = FLAG_DATE
ORDER BY  STATUS_DATE
SID STATUS STATUS_DATE
24 denied 2025-01-06 10:12:33
10 approved 2025-01-19 16:18:52
21 approved 2025-02-12 16:19:27
04 approved 2025-02-27 17:07:17

fiddle

NOTE:
If any of statuses change into approved or denied - the next execution of the code above will work the same regarding the first or last row fetching. That could be the changed row or not.

Explanation

  • with your sample data
SID STATUS STATUS_DATE
21 referred 2025-01-09 08:56:23
21 pended 2025-01-13 08:31:37
21 approved 2025-02-12 16:19:27
10 approved 2025-01-19 16:18:52
10 approved 2025-01-22 07:10:04
24 denied 2025-01-06 10:12:33
04 denied 2025-01-08 01:00:15
04 approved 2025-02-27 17:07:17

... Inner query's Where clause filters out all rows with statuses not approved or denied

If a record has either of approved or denied (refer SID 21 or 24) statjus, then select only that row.

If a record has multiple rows of the same status (refer SID 10), then select the first row.

Case When Count(Distinct STATUS) Over(Partition By SID) = 1
     Then Min(STATUS_DATE) Over(Partition By SID)

...the first condition within Case expression handles both of the above rules (this condition is true for SID 21 and SID 24 and SID 10)

  • If a SID has only approved or only denied status (21 has one approved / SID 24 has one denied) ==> this is the only one and it will get it's own STATUS_DATE as a FLAG_DATE
  • If a SID has only approved or only denied statuses in more than 1 row (10 has two approved) ==> both (all) of them will get the same Min(STATUS_DATE) as a FLAG_DATE

If same SID has different statuses (refer SID 04), then select the last row.

Else Max(STATUS_DATE) Over(Partition By SID)

... the rest is handled by Else clause in the Case expression.

  • If a SID has different (mixed aapproved and denied) statuses (SID 04 has one of each) ==> both (all) of them will get the same Max(STATUS_DATE) as a FLAG_DATE

The inner query results as:

SID STATUS STATUS_DATE FLAG_DATE
04 approved 2025-02-27 17:07:17 2025-02-27 17:07:17
04 denied 2025-01-08 01:00:15 2025-02-27 17:07:17
10 approved 2025-01-19 16:18:52 2025-01-19 16:18:52
10 approved 2025-01-22 07:10:04 2025-01-19 16:18:52
21 approved 2025-02-12 16:19:27 2025-02-12 16:19:27
24 denied 2025-01-06 10:12:33 2025-01-06 10:12:33

fiddle

Now you just have to get the rows with matching STATUS_DATE and FLAG_DATE

Q: Can't import the dump: ERROR 1180 (HY000) at line XXXXX1268: Got error 1 "Operation not permitted" during COMMIT A:

I encountered the same problem when exporting and importing a MySQL database from a very old CentOS Linux release 7.8.2003 VPS to a new Debian 13.3.

I solved it by exporting the dump using the --skip-extended-insert parameter.

Q: Determine function name from within that function A:

implementing your own decorator

#foo.py

from mydecorators import *

@print_my_name
def bar():
    #do something else
    pass

bar()  # this will print `my name is: bar`

#mydecorators.py

def resolve_function(func):
    #in case annotated func is an staticmethod
    if isinstance(func,staticmethod):
        return func.__func__
    return func

def print_my_name(func):
    def function_caller(*args,**kwargs):
        _func = resolve_function(func)
        print("my name is: %s" %_func.__name__)
        return _func(*args,**kwargs)
    return function_caller

Q: Cereal serialization of inherited classes doesn't work A:

I figured it out! tysm @abcdefg

the real problem was actually that i was mixing up save/load functions with inherited classes. In my actual code, Component had a serialize function while Script and ExampleScript had a save/load function which will cause cereal to throw that error without any extra details.

What fixed it for the code example I provided was removing the base class in the archive function (the base class had nothing to archive anyways)

Q: Calling Firebase Messaging through Functions throws unknown error A:

If you look in the HTML, the error message is:

The requested URL /batch was not found on this server

That /batch endpoint was part of the legacy FCM API, which was deprecated multiple years ago and was removed over a year ago.

Most likely you're using a very old SDK that still tries to call this endpoint. To fix the problem, move to a newer SDK that calls the new endpoints and update your code for any relevant API changes.

Also see my answer from January last year to a Java user: Facing difficulty in multicast push notification in java spring boot

Q: general about the carrier pursuing A:

honestly dont overthink which language should i start with there isnt one perfect language the right choice depends on what you want to build if you want to build websites start with javascript if you are interested in ai or machine learning start with python if you like low level stuff performance or game engines then c++ is a good option if you are completely unsure python is usually the safest and most beginner friendly start

about mastering a language you dont master it by watching tons of tutorials or collecting certificates you master it by building things learn the basics first like variables loops functions and conditionals then start building small projects you will get stuck you will make mistakes you will debug for hours that is normal that is actually how you improve after small projects move to bigger ones read other peoples code maybe contribute to open source and slowly dive into more advanced topics mastery comes from time consistency and real problem solving not passive learning

for materials use structured and trusted sources free platforms like freecodecamp the odin project for web and cs50 by harvard are great official documentation is also very important even if it feels hard at first on youtube follow proper playlists instead of random videos books are underrated too like automate the boring stuff with python or eloquent javascript depending on the language

what you should do next is simple pick one language and stick to it spend the first month learning the fundamentals and practicing daily in the second month build a few small projects like a calculator a todo app or a simple website or cli tool in the third month build one bigger project and put it on github also learn git properly

if you want to be really good focus on fundamentals learn data structures and algorithms understand how the internet works and get comfortable with debugging dont avoid hard problems the first language you choose will not matter much in the long run what matters is consistency depth of understanding and your ability to solve problems
